key_insight: τ-Knowledge provides a realistic, integrated benchmark that evaluates conversational agents on their ability to retrieve and apply domain-specific knowledge from large unstructured corpora during long-horizon, live interactions—closing the gap between isolated retrieval and tool-use evaluations.
problem_solved: Existing benchmarks test retrieval or tool use separately and fail to capture end-to-end agent behavior over unstructured data in prolonged dialogues; τ-Knowledge addresses this by offering a unified, agentic evaluation framework for knowledge-intensive conversational settings.
method: Extend τ-Bench into τ-Knowledge to create end-to-end evaluation scenarios where agents must access large, proprietary, unstructured corpora during multi-turn conversations.
Define interactive tasks and an evaluation protocol that measure retrieval accuracy, grounding, answer correctness, and long-horizon consistency in live exchanges.
Combine automated metrics and human judgments to capture compositional failures (retrieval → reasoning → response) and enable comparisons across retrieval-augmented and tool-using agent designs.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical benchmark to diagnose and improve agent grounding, retrieval integration, and long-term conversational reliability in real-world, knowledge-intensive domains—accelerating safer and more accurate deployed assistants.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user ↔ agent ↔ retrieval over unstructured corpus (highlighting retrieval + tool modules and response generation).
Interaction timeline: multi-turn dialogue showing when retrievals occur, when tools are used, and where failures/contradictions arise.
Metric dashboard: side-by-side bar/heatmap comparing retrieval accuracy, grounding score, and end-to-end answer correctness across models.
Case example flow: annotated conversation excerpt showing source passages, grounding links, and final agent response (true vs. hallucinated parts).
paper_title: $τ$-Knowledge: Evaluating Conversational Agents over Unstructured Knowledge
paper_authors: Quan Shi, Alexandra Zytek, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan, Victor Barres
